actions.text: Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs. Ordered to be reported with an amendment in the nature of a substitute favorably.
Read twice and referred to the Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs.

committees.name: Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committee

dimensions.assessment: Affects all federal agencies that issue or review permits, as well as any citizens, businesses, or entities applying for federal permits.
dimensions.evidence: The head of each covered agency shall include on the website of the covered agency a webpage that displays information relating to the status of an application

dimensions.assessment: Provides administrative transparency and tracking data for permit applicants, improving visibility without altering underlying permit laws.
dimensions.evidence: a description of the stages completed by the covered agency or any reviewing agency in the application review process

dimensions.assessment: The source material mentions no specific federal spending, appropriations, or economic costs.
Imposes a new website disclosure mandate on all federal agencies that issue permits or participate in permit reviews.
dimensions.evidence: The term 'covered agency' means an agency that issues permits.

dimensions.assessment: Permanent ongoing requirement for federal permitting agencies to maintain and update permit application web pages.
dimensions.evidence: include on the website of the covered agency a webpage that displays information relating to the status of an application

missing_information: Cost estimates or administrative burdens for agencies to build and maintain the required webpages.
importance_detail.rationale: The bill requires federal agencies that issue permits to maintain a dedicated website displaying detailed tracking information, review statuses, and contact details for individual permit applications.
